title: Requires Any Role
prompt: A TypeScript route guard receives the current user roles and the roles allowed for a route. Write a function that returns true when the user has at least one allowed role.

explanation.beginner:
Example: requiresAnyRole(["admin","editor"], ["admin"]) produces true. The result must follow this precise rule: A TypeScript route guard receives the current user roles and the roles allowed for a route. Write a function that returns true when the user has at least one allowed role. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “rejects missing roles”: input [["viewer"],["admin","editor"]] produces false. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
